headline: Blind Chimp Sees Again After Historic Cataract Surgery
meta_description: Pierre, a 54-year-old chimpanzee at Chimp Haven sanctuary in Louisiana, regains sight after the facility's first cataract surgery, reconnecting with caregivers…
summary_short: A 54-year-old chimpanzee named Pierre has regained his sight following cataract surgery at Chimp Haven, the world's largest chimpanzee sanctuary in Louisiana.
body:
Pierre, a 54-year-old chimpanzee at Chimp Haven in Northwest Louisiana, is seeing again. After becoming completely blind from cataracts, the aging resident underwent surgery—the first of its kind at the world's largest chimpanzee sanctuary—and within hours began responding visually to a longtime caregiver. Within days, he had reunited with Jill, one of his closest chimpanzee companions, and returned to his social group earlier than expected. The restoration of functional sight has allowed Pierre to reconnect with the people, chimpanzees, and familiar activities that define his daily life. Colony Director Michelle Reininger, who has known and cared for Pierre for more than 25 years, said of the moment he saw her again: "Watching Pierre look at me again was something I will never forget."

What made Pierre's recovery possible was not the surgery alone, but months of meticulous preparation. Staff trained Pierre using positive reinforcement to voluntarily present his eyes for care—teaching him to accept eyedrops and positioning for monitoring while he was still blind. Caregivers also adapted his environment with sound cues, specialized feeding approaches, handholds, and ladders to help him navigate independently as his vision declined. Board-certified veterinary ophthalmologist Dr. Kenneth Pierce performed the procedure, while the broader care team ensured Pierre would be comfortable with any follow-up treatment needed.

Pierre's case reflects Chimp Haven's philosophy of individualized aging care. "Every chimpanzee ages differently, just like people do," said Dr. DaShaunté Coleman, the sanctuary's veterinarian. "Our goal is to understand what each individual needs and help them remain comfortable, active and connected to their social group as they age." Founded in 2000 on 200 wooded acres in Caddo Parish, Chimp Haven emerged as a response to the closure of medical research programs that had long subjected chimpanzees to captive breeding and testing. Today, the sanctuary provides hundreds of retired research chimpanzees with enriched lives and sophisticated medical care—care like what restored Pierre's sight and his place among those who love him.
quick_facts: Pierre: 54-year-old chimpanzee at Chimp Haven sanctuary
Location: 200-acre facility in Northwest Louisiana, founded 2000
First cataract surgery performed at the world's largest chimp sanctuary
Recovery included months of positive reinforcement training beforehand
Within days, Pierre reunited with companion Jill in his social group
